title: The ASEAN Paradox
gist: Paywalled teaser: Thitinan Pongsudhirak argues that ahead of its 60th anniversary and the Manila summit (Nov 16–18), ASEAN is more divided and less effective than ever, and must turn its convening authority into concerted action or be reduced to an arena for great-power rivalry.

insights.claim: On the eve of its 60th anniversary, ASEAN is more divided and less effective than ever, with several rifts exposing its institutional shortcomings despite outward displays of unity at the Manila summit on November 16–18.
insights.speaker: Thitinan Pongsudhirak
insights.so_what: A weaker ASEAN reduces Southeast Asia's collective leverage in trade and security disputes.
insights.quote: the group is more divided and less effective than ever
insights.locator: BANGKOK—When Southeast Asia’s leaders link arms

insights.claim: Amid a fracturing global order, ASEAN must either turn its convening authority into concerted action or be reduced to an arena for great-power rivalry.
insights.speaker: Thitinan Pongsudhirak
insights.so_what: Watch whether Southeast Asia becomes a contested US-China battleground, raising regional geopolitical risk for investors.
insights.quote: turn its convening authority into concerted action or be reduced to an arena for great-power rivalry
